primary_text.read: FOBU12018 record and caption, not modern growth habit as fossil evidence.

Manchester and Zavada 1987 description and figures 1–11 captions: variable palmate blunt laminae, thin lobe midveins and open dichotomizing secondary venation, nonlaminar branched fertile portions. No claim exact vein reconstruction, no microscopic spores.

lygodium.observations: Personally viewed entire NPS fossil photograph: continuous bifid blade, blunt elongate lobes, deep cleft, small fertile portion at shared narrow base. The final is an abstract display interpretation of these organs, not a whole climbing plant. Veins are simplified forked relief; the real taxon has thin lobe midveins and secondary veins, not an assertion that midveins are absent.
lygodium.limits: 1987 article text and original captions read; article plate raster not acquired. NPS actual photograph is the pixel basis.

primary_text.read: Original authors institutional report; the compression photos and proposed living conic reconstruction are distinct.

Wan et al. 2020 pre-proof, emended diagnosis on printed p6: closely bundled unbranched filaments radiate from basal attachment, often preserved as fan-shaped compressions; affinity ambiguous. Indexed PDF text uses shifted character encoding but the diagnostic sentences are readable. Screenshot attempts failed, no primary plate pixel claim.

flabellophyton.observations: Personally viewed full institutional composite. Left two Lantian specimens are long narrow fans with close fine radiating striation and slender bases. The rightmost green cone is an interpretation, not the selected specimen. Final is compressed and rootless with integrated stalk, not a live cone or branching seaweed.
flabellophyton.limits: The frozen reference display title for WAN2020_PRIMARY is incorrect. Correct title is A tale of three taphonomic modes: The Ediacaran fossil Flabellophyton preserved in limestone, black shale, and sandstone. DOI 10.1016/j.gr.2020.04.003, authors, year and journal/page range point to the correct inspected work. Nonblocking citation-title correction recommended as append-only metadata; do not alter original freeze.

primary_text.read: Dawson 1888 original bilobata description and Fig16B: oval/reniform, paired rounded prominences and central depression, 3–6mm. Historical sporocarp/water-fern interpretation not adopted.

Schopf and Schwietering 1970 introduction, conclusion and plate captions. Important scope: illustrated plates are Foerstia ohioensis, and authors distinguish it from Protosalvinia; this is related comparative texture/context, not direct P. bilobata specimen proof.

protosalvinia.observations: Personally inspected entire Fig16 and selected only upper B bodies, not A/C/D spore-like diagrams. Personally inspected museum printed p66 and Fig6c: a dark oval compression; lobing too indistinct to use as precise contour. Final isolated bilobed body is anchored to Dawson B, not the old biological assignment.
protosalvinia.limits: USGS plates not seen. Do not relabel USGS Foerstia plate 1 as P. bilobata. Museum photograph is supplemental and its age label is not used. Cancellate relief is illustrative, not an observed cell-size reconstruction.

primary_text.read: Whitfield 1894 printed pp355–356 and PlateXI11–13; slender plume and spaced fine whorls from Trenton Wisconsin.

LoDuca, Melchin and Verbruggen 2011 printed pp12–14: Chaetocladus architecture has undivided axis and whorled unbranched laterals; C. plumula explicitly Ordovician Wisconsin. C. capitatus dimensions/cap not imported.

chaetocladus.observations: Personally viewed whole original PlateXI, distinguishing 11–12 from neighboring taxa and obsolete apparent fork/joint Fig13. Final one-order filaments and single axis are the revised interpretation; not Silurian, not a dendritic hierarchy.
chaetocladus.limits: 2019 full text not obtained or claimed reviewed. The scope does not claim exhaustive current taxonomic review.

scientific_policy: Concepts are art direction, not taxonomic evidence. Frozen organ scopes and broad authored dimensions retained. No new microscopic or arbitrary percentage gates.
